findings.title: Migration SQL tests miss case-insensitive key
findings.problem: Which rows are deleted is decided entirely in _SELECT_ROWS/_DELETE_ORPHANS, but no test executes them: _ScriptedBind feeds precomputed match flags and a synthetic rowcount (len(ids)). The SQL checks are substrings only: test_select_matches_id_and_name_case_insensitively asserts 'LOWER(' appears anywhere (satisfied by LOWER(id)), and test_delete_rechecks_no_match asserts no LOWER at all. Removing LOWER() from up.project_name in either statement passes every test. No live-PostgreSQL harness exists in the repo.
findings.impact: Consumer is every deployment upgrading past e5f9a1c3b7d2 against production user_projects. A regression in the case-insensitive comparison would classify case-only rows (e.g. 'MyTeam' for application 'myteam', the IDP bootstrap case the spec keeps) as orphans and delete them irreversibly, with downgrade a no-op and no backup, while the suite stays green.
findings.recommendation: In test_select_matches_id_and_name_case_insensitively assert `LOWER(up.project_name) IN (SELECT LOWER(id)` and `UNION SELECT LOWER(name)` are present in _SELECT_ROWS; in test_delete_rechecks_no_match assert `LOWER(up.project_name) NOT IN (SELECT LOWER(id)` and `UNION SELECT LOWER(name)` are present in _DELETE_ORPHANS, so removing either side of the case-insensitive comparison fails a test. Optionally let _ScriptedBind take a rowcount override so the re-check partial-delete path is exercised.
